_about: Which component each verified vault file is quoted for, and what the reading of it says to do.
Hand-written on purpose: this is the judgement step, and it is the part a reader should be able
to disagree with in a diff. vault/eyeball.py decides what a picture shows; this says which
specimen it is evidence about. A verified file absent from here is quoted for nothing --
usually because it is a counter-example for the rules page rather than a model.

fake-os-loaders--blob.gifcities.org_gifc.reading: A marker crosses a named lane at a constant rate (0.70 of the frame travelled, 0.46 of the way at half duration) while the ends and the ground never move (4 of 12 grid cells dead). The library's level should read the same way: extent first, furniture still.

spinner-console--blob.gifcities.org_gifc.reading: The head reaches its far end early (1.0 of the way by half duration) and what remains is the drawn route. A trace that eases out and then holds is a thing that arrived; one that keeps moving has not.

tron-disc--blob.gifcities.org_gifcities_.reading: One ink travels and the trail it leaves stays drawn (1.22 frame-widths covered, mild back-loading). The history of the path is the picture, which is what a trace is for and what a shimmer is not.

rig--blob.gifcities.org_gifcities_2RO5SN.reading: A survey grid with fixed corner labels in which only the contact and a lit region change. The furniture-versus-contact split the library keeps relearning is the whole of this reference.

hologlobe--blob.gifcities.org_gifcities_.reading: Mesh over land, monochrome, constant rotation, no return to frame zero inside the sampled window. No pins and no labels: the rotation carries the whole claim, so the pin paint in globe has to survive the kill switch on its own merits.
Rendered Earth, 0.37 of the frame crossed at a constant rate over 4.2s. The rate is the spec: a hologlobe that accelerates is a graphic, one that is constant is an instrument.
Hue cycle with no measured travel at all -- the instrument and the eye agree independently that nothing moves but the palette. Held as the caution against colour-only distinctions.

motion-tracker--blob.gifcities.org_gifci.reading: Front-loaded tilt (0.93 of the way by half duration, then it holds): a beam tips fast and the load corrects. admission draws exactly this and should not ease in.

fake-os-loaders--blob.gifcities.org_gifc.reading: Counter-example, not model: a word rotating 360 degrees and a dot orbiting it, 2.4s loop. Nothing measured, everything moving -- the exact idiom the chrome rule forbids, which makes it the picture to put next to the rule.
Counter-example: the ellipsis that grows to three dots and cycles. Measured travel 0.043 of a frame -- the only quantity on screen is the dot count, and it says nothing about anything.

cyberpunk-hud--media.tenor.com_gdhPO38Xj.reading: Full-frame game interface: nameplates and segmented health bars ride above a squad, a selection ring breathes on the chosen unit, and a party panel opens at the right with a grid of portrait cells. Two readings, one on each side of the library's rule. The panel arrives over a field that KEEPS RUNNING — health changes, contacts move — which is why an arriving record set is honest there; `dossier` answers "which exact thing am I about to command" from facts already true at read time, so it has no live field, and its stillness is the same rule seen from the other side. The breathing ring is an ambient pulse with no quantity behind it: the selection idiom this app may not put in its chrome, which makes the file a counter-example as well as a map of the idiom.

f16-hud-gcas.gif.reading: A limit that acts, drawn by people who had to fly the thing. FLYUP arrives when the measured closure violates the limit, holds exactly as long as the violation lasts, and is gone the moment it is not; beside it the limit itself is printed (AL 500) with the live value above it, so the cue names the number it is protecting — `envelope`'s 0.62 has to answer to a limit like that or it means nothing. The tapes are the extent idiom `tape` is missing: the graduations scroll and the boxed current value is pinned, so the reading is the MOVEMENT of the scale and the position is the number. Where a value cannot be had the display prints xxx in the field rather than deleting it, and the masked block at lower left keeps its space with every neighbour still laid out — the same refusal the library writes, from the outside. The clock (17:26:17 → 17:26:29) and the countdown counter are the only unambiguous `elapsed` in the frame: both keep counting and neither animates.

scope-envelope-violin.gif.reading: An audio editor: the waveform IS the measurement, the playhead is the only motion, and the motion is a position reading across an axis that is already fully drawn. That is the idiom `tape` and `stripChart` need and do not have — a series that exists as ink along a named lane while a marker crosses it, not a line that grows into being. Note what does NOT move: the ruler, the track labels, the selection block, the waveform behind the head. And note the violin track's shape: a fast attack, a long low tail, which is what a `decay` looks like when it is measured rather than eased.

sweep-hearing-range.gif.reading: A frequency sweep: oscillation rate climbs monotonically and the amplitude ramps in, with no interface furniture anywhere in the file. It is honest to use it only for what it shows — a rate that changes because a measured frequency changes, and an attack that arrives over a fraction of the window rather than all of it. It cannot license anything about frames, labels or readouts, because it has none. Recorded here so the next reader does not mistake a plot of a signal for an interface.

solari-departure-flap.gif.reading: The dispatch board is the dispatch queue, built in 1960s electromechanics, and it settles three arguments this library keeps having. (1) A change arrives by FLIP, never by fade: a character is one of a fixed set of faces and there is no in-between state to render, which is what `hardCut` is for and what an eased reveal on a value change is not. (2) Only the cells whose value changed move — the destination labels and column heads are ink, not animation, so movement reports and everything else rests. (3) Absence is a CHARACTER: a blank flap occupies the cell, holds its position and takes the same time to arrive as a digit, rather than deleting the field and letting the row shrink. And note the two inks for two mechanisms: the clock is red seven-segment, the board is white on black flaps — nothing about a difference is carried by hue alone here, each ink belongs to a different physical claim. CAVEAT, recorded because it inflates any rate read from this file: the camera is handheld and the frame drifts, so `travel of the bright head` includes camera motion the board did not make.

hurricane-irma-radar-loop.gif.reading: A rolling loop, not a repeating one — the only file in the vault that teaches that difference. Measured over 25 frames and 4.17s, the loop shows no return to frame zero: the window rolls forward and the wrap back to the oldest step is a discontinuity, not an ease. The step interval is an eye-read off the contact sheet rather than a file measurement — the stamp on the plate counts forward by six minutes and holds each stamp for several frames, so the age of the picture is printed on the frame it describes. That is the first demand on `radar`: a loop names the interval it steps by, and wraps as a jump. Measured next, 0 of 12 cells still by the bright-ink tracker, which must not be read as the plate moving: that instrument is documented blind to dark ink on a light ground, and the plate's furniture — state outlines, the colour legend, the stamp — is exactly that, so their stillness is an eye-read and labelled as one here. That is the demand on `coverage`: the plate and its legend are untouched by the animation, and a claim of 'nothing is still' belongs to the instrument, not to the picture. Measured last, one saturated ink sits at 0.25 of its final extent at half the duration — front-loaded, because a new observation step appears at full reflectivity instead of growing into itself — while the bright head travels 0.471 of the frame, back-loaded and not monotone, because what is being tracked does not travel in a straight line and the centroid wanders. That is the demand on `tracker`: a value entering the plate is already drawn at its measured value, not faded up to it.

barcode-scan-receipt.gif.reading: A real receipt arriving on screen, and a real wait. Measured: 24 frames over 4.0s, median delay 170.0ms, loop no return to frame zero. This is handheld phone footage pointed at a shop shelf, so the travel and amplitude columns belong to the cameraperson and are not quoted as rates — what the file can hold a component to is its state vocabulary, read off the frames with the eye and labelled as such here. Three states replace one another in place: a viewfinder carrying the reticle and the instruction to point at a barcode; a card saying the code was found and that data is being retrieved, with NO progress bar, no percentage, no remaining-time claim; then a confirmation card naming the product, its price, and a cart badge that steps from 26 to 27. Of `killmail`: a charge record arrives already priced — the amount is on the record itself, next to the thing it charges for, with a running total that moves by exactly that record, so a receipt that prints an amount and separately denies holding one is not a form this display ever has. Of `hardCut`: three states, no in-between drawn, and the counter changes by its increment in a single step. Of `tape`: the wait is the finding — the app knows it does not know how long the lookup takes, and says so in words instead of drawing a bar, which is the difference between an indeterminate wait and a lie about a determinate one.
